sentences.text: Bacteroides fragilis is described as a key member of the human gut microbiota that contributes to host health by maintaining intestinal homeostasis.
The same study notes it is the most frequently isolated anaerobe in clinical infections, and reported that infection-associated isolates spanned all phylogroups, indicating no pathogenic lineage.
That analysis of 813 genomes identified 16 phylogroups, distinguished by genes associated with capsule biosynthesis and interbacterial competition.
Another study reported that Bacteroides fragilis and its secreted outer membrane vesicles induced autophagy, which facilitated clearance of Pseudomonadota in macrophages.
A community-level analysis of 274 stool metagenomes from older adults reported Bacteroides fragilis enriched in Alzheimer's disease.
